title: BDC leads investment in Saskatoon company modernizing railway logistics | BetaKit
html:
Saskatoon’s Standard Rail Corporation has raised $1.85 million to scale its railway logistics platform, the company announced last week.

The news: Standard Rail announced the seed investment on Nov. 12, telling BetaKit that the funding was led by BDC’s Capital Seed Venture Fund, with additional participation from Waterloo’s Infiniq Ventures. Funding will go toward expanding the company’s logistics platform, SIDINGS, as well as growing its engineering and marketing teams.

From the source: “I spent years driving industrial roads looking for track, knocking on doors for storage and transload, and icing it together one site at a time,” said Standard Rail CEO Robert Skarzynski in a press release. “With BDC’s backing, we’re building the system this industry has always needed.”

The context: SIDINGS is designed as a digital platform connecting domestic and international shippers with rail capacity across North America. The platform is intended to replicate the ease-of-access logistics that has become commonplace in both the air and ocean freight industries but has remained largely disconnected in the broader rail transportation industry. The platform is an open network service connecting shippers, facilities, and rail service providers in a single online location. Shippers can search for more than 60,000 rail-served locations in Canada, Mexico, and the United States. The platform also allows users to book, bid, and request pricing online.

Standard Rail said that with BDC’s financing, it will look to onboard more rail service providers to the platform.

Final thought: Prior to launching SIDINGS, Standard Rail was involved in physical railcar maintenance, repair, and fleet services, including logistics planning, which gave the company’s team a frontline view of the rail transportation industry. It was that domain knowledge that Mark Smith, partner and team lead at BDC’s Seed Venture Fund, said clinched the bank’s decision to back Standard Rail, which has several competitors that also service the rail logistics space, including Commtrex and Canadian rival Freightera. Smith called Standard Rail’s hands-on involvement in the industry a strategic advantage as it seeks to scale.
